title: The lowest place (Luke 14:7–14)
hook: sit at the bottom of the table, and invite those who can't repay
carry: invite the ones who can't repay

segments.voice: Yesterday, a hen spread her wings over a city that wouldn't come. Your line was under her wings. What did you shelter? Day four hundred sixty-eight.

Every wedding reception has a seating chart, and everyone checks it. Table one, near the couple: family and the best friends. Table twelve, by the kitchen door: the coworkers and the plus-ones nobody's met. People notice where they land, and some people quietly move their place card. Jesus is at a dinner on the sabbath, in the house of a leading Pharisee, and he's watching the guests do exactly this: angling for the best couches near the host. So he gives them some advice. Today, the lowest place.
screen: `EVERYONE CHECKS THE SEATING CHART.` → `TABLE TWELVE, BY THE KITCHEN.` → `GUESTS ANGLING FOR THE BEST SEATS.`

segments.voice: First, to the guests. Don't grab the top seat, he says. Someone more honored may arrive, and the host will ask you to move, and you'll walk the whole room to the bottom in front of everybody. "But when thou art invited, go, sit down in the lowest place." Then the host may come and say: friend, go up higher, and you'll be honored in front of the whole table. It sounds like good manners, and it is. The Book of Proverbs gives almost the same advice about standing before a king. But Jesus ends with a line that goes past manners: "every one that exalteth himself, shall be humbled; and he that humbleth himself, shall be exalted." Then he turns to the host. When you give a dinner, don't invite your friends, your brothers, your relatives or your rich neighbors, because they'll invite you back, and that's your repayment. Instead: "call the poor, the maimed, the lame, and the blind; And thou shalt be blessed, because they have not wherewith to make thee recompense." That's the harder half. A dinner party in that world, like a lot of social life now, ran on exchange. You invite me, I invite you. Jesus says: break the loop. Invite the people who can't pay you back, and let God do the repaying, at the resurrection of the just. The two halves fit together. As a guest, don't measure your worth by your seat. As a host, don't measure your guests by what they can give. Catholics hear this as more than etiquette. The Mass itself is a supper where nobody earned a seat, and every one of us came in as a guest who couldn't repay.
screen: `DON'T GRAB THE TOP SEAT.` · `FRIEND, GO UP HIGHER.` · `HE THAT HUMBLETH HIMSELF.` · `CALL THE POOR, THE LAME, THE BLIND.` · then, large: `SIT DOWN IN THE LOWEST PLACE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: take the lower seat. Settle, and breathe. Think through today's rooms: a meeting, a meal, a line, a group chat, a car. Where would you usually take the better place: the first word, the best chair, the last slice, the credit? Pick one place today where you'll take the lower one instead, on purpose and quietly. Picture yourself doing it. Notice how it feels: a little uncomfortable, maybe, and a little free. If you pray, ask for a humble heart. The bell holds the time.
The lowest place. Jesus' advice at a dinner: take the bottom seat, and when you host, invite the ones who can't repay. Today's word.
Your line: invite the ones who can't repay. Today, take one lower seat, and think about who you could invite this month who could never invite you back. Day four hundred sixty-eight.

howItsDone: Catholic parishes and communities such as the Catholic Worker and the Community of Sant'Egidio hold meals where the poor are guests at the table, not just recipients of food, taking Luke 14 as their pattern.

fork.setup: you arrive at a big dinner. the best seats near the host are still empty. where do you sit?
options: near the host, before someone else takes it.
fork.reveal: Jesus says sit in the lowest place, so the host may say friend, go up higher, and you'll be honored.

original.note: Greek: the last place, the lowest seat at the table.

trapdoor: what you thought: this is a tip for looking humble so you get promoted.
what it means: Jesus asks guests not to measure their worth by their seat, and hosts to invite people who can't repay.
what a scholar hears: meals in that world ran on reciprocity and honor; Jesus moves the repayment to the resurrection of the just.
